avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inducer reduces tacrolimus levels significantly, leading to subtherapeutic concentrations and transplant rejection risk
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; discontinue immediately if currently used and monitor tacrolimus levels closely

avoid_supplements.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit Juice
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibitor dramatically increases tacrolimus bioavailability and toxicity risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid completely; counsel patient to eliminate from diet

avoid_supplements.name: Echinacea
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inducer may reduce tacrolimus concentrations and increase rejection risk
avoid_supplements.action: Advise against use; recommend alternative immune support if needed

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic supplements (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction may decrease tacrolimus levels
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose garlic supplements; moderate dietary garlic acceptable

caution_supplements.name: Milk thistle
caution_supplements.mechanism: May induce CYP3A4 metabolism; potential for modest tacrolimus level reduction
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; monitor tacrolimus levels if initiated or discontinued

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin
caution_supplements.mechanism: May inhibit CYP3A4 at high doses; potential for level increase
caution_supplements.action: Limit to dietary amounts; avoid therapeutic supplements without monitoring

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition increases tacrolimus concentrations 2-3 fold, elevating toxicity risk
avoid_foods.action: Complete avoidance required; educate patient on hidden sources (some juices, pomelo)

avoid_foods.name: Pomelo/Seville oranges
avoid_foods.mechanism: Similar furanocoumarins as grapefruit; potent CYP3A4 inhibition
avoid_foods.action: Avoid completely; counsel on citrus variety awareness

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase tacrolimus absorption variability; food effect depends on formulation
caution_foods.action: Maintain consistent dietary patterns; take with or without food consistently per formulation guidance

caution_foods.name: Cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, cabbage)
caution_foods.mechanism: Potential CYP3A4 induction with very high intake
caution_foods.action: Normal dietary intake acceptable; avoid excessive supplementation

monitoring_notes: Tacrolimus has a narrow therapeutic window (10-20 ng/mL) and high CYP3A4/3A5 metabolism making drug interactions clinically significant. Obtain baseline and periodic tacrolimus trough levels, especially when any supplements or significant dietary changes are initiated, and monitor renal function and signs of toxicity (tremor, headache, hyperglycemia).
